name: heralded-memory
question: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time did each report?

Q0.label: main
Q0.text: Which experiments have demonstrated heralded entanglement between two remote quantum memories, and what herald rate, Bell-state fidelity and storage time did each report?
Q0.keywords: heralded entanglement remote quantum memories experiment herald rate Bell state fidelity storage time

Q1.label: subject
Q1.text: Two physically separated quantum memory nodes, such as trapped ions, neutral atoms, atomic ensembles, NV or SiV colour centres in diamond, or rare-earth-doped crystals, connected by optical photons.
Q1.keywords: quantum memory nodes trapped ion neutral atom atomic ensemble NV SiV diamond rare-earth crystal photon

Q2.label: approach
Q2.text: Entanglement is heralded by interfering photons emitted by each memory at a middle station and detecting one or two photons, as in Barrett-Kok, DLCZ or single-click schemes.
Q2.keywords: heralding photon interference beam splitter Bell state measurement single-click two-photon Barrett-Kok DLCZ

Q3.label: outcome
Q3.text: Reported figures of merit: entanglement generation or herald rate per second, fidelity to the target Bell state, and memory storage or coherence time compared with the time needed to herald.
Q3.keywords: entanglement rate success probability Bell state fidelity memory coherence time storage time

Q4.label: context
Q4.text: Nodes sit in separate laboratories or buildings and are linked over deployed or spooled optical fibre, often after conversion to telecom wavelengths.
Q4.keywords: separate laboratories deployed fiber kilometres metropolitan link telecom frequency conversion
